deploy.label: Update
deploy.description: Updates the bot (git pull + rebuild). Owner only.
deploy.notOwner: ❌ Only the bot owner can trigger an update.
deploy.title: 🚀 Bot update
deploy.intro: Confirm to run `git pull` then the Docker rebuild on the host.
deploy.requested: 🚀 Update of **`{branch}`** requested. The host will pull and rebuild — the bot will restart shortly.
deploy.requestFailed: ❌ Couldn't write the update request (check `DEPLOY_DIR` and permissions).
deploy.restartedNoResult: ✅ Bot restarted. The update result is not available yet.
deploy.requestNotPicked:
⚠️ The host updater has not picked up the request yet. Last state: {status}
Check that `vakzbot-updater.sh loop` is running or that the systemd `.path` watches `DEPLOY_DIR`.
deploy.updateTimeout:
⚠️ No restart or result after {seconds}s. Last state: {status}
Check the host updater logs and Docker Compose.
deploy.updateFailed: ❌ Update failed before restart. Last state: {status}
deploy.updateFinishedNoRestart: ⚠️ The updater finished with `{status}` (commit `{commit}`), but the bot did not restart after {seconds}s. If Docker says "no changes", the image/container was probably not recreated.
deploy.modeFull: 🐢 **Full** — `docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate`: every container of the project is recreated, the bot always restarts.
deploy.modeCache: ⚡ **Fast** — `docker compose up -d --build bot`: Docker reuses its layers, only the `bot` service is targeted, and the container is recreated only if the image really changed. Other containers (flaresolverr, lavalink…) are left alone.
deploy.requestedCache: ⚡ **Fast** update of **`{branch}`** requested. The host reuses the Docker cache: the bot will restart only if the image changed.
deploy.updateFinishedCache: ✅ Update finished with `{status}` (commit `{commit}`) without a restart. In fast mode that is the normal outcome when the image did not change: the bot kept running.
